Asheron's Call on the Darktide server was the peak of sophistication and design.

Very few people saw the magic, and knew the power of what a game could be. I try to teach turbine employees about the old ways when I see them at pax, perhaps one day the successor to AC will come.

The joy of character collision. Having arrows and spells be real dodge-able physical projectiles, the cool portals. The pvp was uber beyond parallel. Being skill based, a few players rose to international fame for their ownsmanship. The loot system allowed you to find a 1 in 10k rare item, and keep it in battle as long as you had drop items to cover it. Lose too many drop items however, and you could lose your cool stuff based upon it;s gold value. But.. you could get lucky too.

High risk, high reward. Actual adrenaline.

Botting and combat macros also formented, reaching sophistication that cannot be expressed in what little space we have here.

Political ideologies... guilds allied with each other sharing control of dungeons to keep XP flowing. The Blood guild founded the philosophy of "red is dead". The way of "random player killing" became a dominant force, followed soon by the "Anti"'s, who rose up to oppose the RPK's.

The stories of the duping of the Nexus armor, and hacking of the KOS guild read like Greek Epics.

Now compare that to Wow, the one dimensional grind-fest.

I would be great to see something written up like a novel from the players points of view on some of the great server wide tales that happen in MMOs, Sounds like Asheron's Call would have some good ones and there would be some from EVE's great heists/betrayals as well that would be cool to read that way.
Thats an exciting idea, it's easier than ever to self publish these days... you might be able to load a file up into a website to make a printable book.

Sadly I have neither the knowledge nor the writing skills to put together something like this. It would need a good writer and having access to get information about the events from a fair selection of players involved in the events.
